dfz7nkcpg48xfINSERT INTO GLBTRNVALIDRES(ACMASTCODE, AC_NO, MSGCD, MSGDESCR, WARNINGMSG) SELECT :"SYS_B_00", :"SYS_B_01", :"SYS_B_02", :"SYS_B_03"||NAME||:"SYS_B_04"||ACCNT||:"SYS_B_05"||TOTODAMT, :"SYS_B_06" FROM ( SELECT A.ACCNT, A.TOTODAMT, A.GMST_CODE, B.NAME FROM ( SELECT :"SYS_B_07", :"SYS_B_08", COUNT(DISTINCT B.ACMASTCODE*:"SYS_B_09"+B.AC_NO) AS ACCNT, SUM(DECODE(NVL(B.OVERDUEAMT, :"SYS_B_10"), :"SYS_B_11", NVL(B.PEND_INST, :"SYS_B_12"), NVL(B.OVERDUEAMT, :"SYS_B_13"))) AS TOTODAMT, B.GMST_CODE FROM VIEWLNMAS B WHERE NVL(B.CLOSED, :"SYS_B_14") <> :"SYS_B_15" AND NVL(B.POST, :"SYS_B_16")= :"SYS_B_17" AND B.GMST_CODE=:"SYS_B_18" GROUP BY B.GMST_CODE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT B.ACMASTCODE*:"SYS_B_19"+B.AC_NO)>:"SYS_B_20" ) A , BANKMAS B WHERE A.GMST_CODE=B.GMST_CODE AND NVL(A.TOTODAMT, :"SYS_B_21")>:"SYS_B_22" )

DECODE(GREATEST(NVL(ACCINT, :"SYS_B_051")+NVL(INTAFTMAT, :"SYS_B_052"), :"SYS_B_053"), :"SYS_B_054", ABS(NVL(ACCINT, :"SYS_B_055")+NVL(INTAFTMAT, :"SYS_B_056")), :"SYS_B_057") AS CREDIT,           Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.77 active sessions, 23.42% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.77 active sessions, 23.42% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 1.36 active sessions, 18.02% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .51 active sessions, 6.72% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 6% for SQL execution,
      36% for parsing, 58% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" was executed 184638 times and
      had an average elapsed time of 0.022 seconds.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .25 active sessions, 3.34% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the SELECT statement with SQL_ID "0k8522rmdzg4k" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 0k8522rmdzg4k.
         select privilege# from sysauth$ where (grantee#=:1 or grantee#=1) and
         privilege#>0
   Action
      Use bigger fetch arrays while fetching results from the SELECT statement
      with SQL_ID "0k8522rmdzg4k".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 0k8522rmdzg4k.
         select privilege# from sysauth$ where (grantee#=:1 or grantee#=1) and
         privilege#>0
   Rationale
      The SQL spent only 13% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster
      waits. Therefore, the SQL Tuning Advisor is not applicable in this case.
      Look at performance data for the SQL to find potential improvements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 33% for SQL

   Rationale

Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.28 active sessions, 16.87% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.28 active sessions, 16.87% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.28 active sessions, 16.87% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 4: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is .37 active sessions, 4.86% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "library cache: mutex X" amounted to 1% of database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 1% of database time.
Waits for "library cache: bucket mutex X" amounted to 1% of database time.

   No recommendations are available.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .41 active sessions, 5.44% of total activity.


Finding 5: Undersized SGA
Impact is .34 active sessions, 4.44% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "102400 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .34 active sessions, 4.44% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      192000 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .72 active sessions, 9.45% of total activity.


Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .34 active sessions, 4.44% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .34 active sessions, 4.44% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .72 active sessions, 9.45% of total activity.
